Ṛtavya
(‘related to the ṛtus’)
------------------------------------------
This is a technical term used to indicate the twelve mantras of the Ṛgveda (2.36 and 37).
Ṛtu means a season. The twelve months of the year are divided into six ṛtus: vasanta (spring), grīṣma (summer), varṣa (rainy season), śarad (autumn), hemanta (fall) and śiśira (winter).
Each of these ṛtus or seasons has an abhimānī-devatā or a presiding deity. A होम or a sacrifice called Ṛtuyājahoma is performed with the help of the above mentioned twelve mantras to please these deities and attain हेअवेन् or other objects like strength, fame, wealth and so on.
Other gods like इन्द्र, अश्विन्स् and Draviṇodā are also requested in these mantras to drink the सोम juice that is offered and give the sacrificer good health as also long life.

ṛtambharaprajñā
(‘truth-bearing चोन्स्चिओउस्नेस्स्’)
------------------------------------------
The Yogasūtras of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.) is the most systematic and basic work of Hindu psychology which deals with the characteristics of a healthy or even a supernormal मिन्द्.
While dealing with समाधि or the superconscious state of मिन्द्, पतञ्जलि has used this word ‘ṛtambharaprajñā’ (1.48).
When the मिन्द् of the योगि (one who is practising meditation as per the directions given by पतञ्जलि) is rid of the impurities of रजस् and तमस्, it learns to flow unhindered, culminating in the experience of the पुरुष or the आत्मन् (the Self).
When such a मिन्द् is directed towards any object, it can give a direct and clear knowledge of that object untainted and unhindered. Hence it is called ṛtambhara-prajñā (a knowledge that is full of the true nature of that object). The समाधि state in which this occurs is called ‘dharmamegha-समाधि’.
See also DHARMAMEGHA-SAMĀDHI and GUṆA.
